item.title: Your Lighthouse score is not your visitors.
item.description:
30-second trick: Your Lighthouse score is not your visitors.
PageSpeed Insights shows two things. The top half is real-user data from the Chrome UX Report over the last 28 days. The score below it is one lab run on a simulated phone.
Try it now: Read the top half first. If your page has no real-user data there, collect your own with Google's web-vitals library.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=field-vs-lab

item.title: Al Jazeera marks text for voice, blocks AI.
item.description:
Its JSON-LD names a NewsMediaOrganization and marks speakable text for voice assistants. Yet robots.txt disallows ChatGPT-User and PerplexityBot, which fetch pages to cite them in AI answers. GEO: 64.
The lesson for every team: Decide crawler by crawler. Training bots and answer bots are separate user-agents, so each can get its own rule.

item.title: DW blocks framing. It skips nosniff.
item.description:
frame-ancestors 'none' stops other sites from framing it, HSTS is on, and every page analyzed has a canonical. But X-Content-Type-Options is missing on all 20 pages analyzed, so browsers may guess file types.
The lesson for every team: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response. One header stops browsers running a file as the wrong type.
One automated analysis of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict. How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-100-2026-11&utm_content=dw

item.title: Skip link: jump straight past the menu.
item.description:
Word of the day: Skip link: jump straight past the menu.
A link at the very top of the page that takes keyboard and screen reader users straight to the main content. It is one way to meet WCAG 2.4.1, Bypass Blocks, at Level A.
Spot it: Load your page and press Tab once. The first thing that appears should be a way to skip to the content.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=skip-link

item.title: Can anyone send mail as your domain?
item.description:
30-second trick: Can anyone send mail as your domain?
A DMARC record tells receiving servers what to do with mail that claims your domain but fails authentication. Without one, spoofed mail has an easier way in.
Try it now: Run the lookup on your domain. No answer? Publish p=none with a report address, read the reports, then move to quarantine.
